question.prompt: There is more than one integer greater than \(1\) which, when divided by any integer \(k\) such that \(2\le k\le11,\) has a remainder of \(1.\) What is the difference between the two smallest such integers?

solutions.explanation:
Let \(N>1\) be an integer satisfying the conditions. Having remainder \(1\) when divided by each integer from \(2\) through \(11\) means that \(N-1\) is a positive multiple of every one of these divisors. Thus we need their least common multiple.

For each prime, take the largest power needed by any divisor in the list. These powers are \(2^3\), \(3^2\), \(5\), \(7\), and \(11\). Their product contains every required prime factor, so
\[
L=\operatorname{lcm}(2,3,\ldots,11)
=2^3\cdot3^2\cdot5\cdot7\cdot11
=27{,}720.
\]
Every admissible integer therefore has the form \(1+tL\), where \(t\) is a positive integer. Conversely, each such integer leaves remainder \(1\) for every allowed divisor, since \(1<k\).

The two smallest occur at \(t=1\) and \(t=2\), giving \(27{,}721\) and \(55{,}441\). Their difference is \(\boxed{27{,}720}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
solutions.title: Subtract 1 and find the common multiple
